direction: Evolve score_ruin_nodes toward a scale-normalized, capacity-and-stagnation-adaptive removal priority that targets nodes from over-full / long routes (tight-capacity regime) while decaying toward worst-cost removal when time is plentiful.

operations.mechanism: Round 2 already improved mean objective to 16.0201 ms=172ms of the 500ms budget, so there is ~3x time headroom but only 0.19% gap to VBS — the remaining gain must come from better ruin *targeting*, not more iterations. KB method-cvrp-m3-ruin-recreate-l3 confirms the evolved-hook (vs Worst-Cost L3-ctrl) route is the proven lever on this template, and method-cvrp-lns-shaw-regret supports mixing worst-cost (removal_savings) with relatedness/structure terms. The weakest regimes reported are capacity_level=tight, depot_style=eccentric and size=100, motivating explicit route_load_frac and route_dist_share features in the score. All terms are normalized by the global depot-distance scale per method-cvrp-m2-l2a-generalized-savings / method-cvrp-frozen-c-near-tie to guarantee scale invariance and avoid the documented mixed-unit near-tie blow-up. Postprocess stays 'none' as the only allowed mode.

preserve: Route feasibility, strict time budget, and scale invariance.
hypothesis: A removal priority of the form score_i = removal_savings_i/scale * (1 + beta*route_load_frac_i^2) * (1 + gamma*route_dist_share_i) with scale = mean(d(0,1..n)) keeps the hook dimensionless (no O(1/s^2) scale collapse, cf. method-cvrp-frozen-c-near-tie), and biasing toward routes with load near/over capacity plus high distance share removes the customers whose reinsertion Regret-2 can actually restructure — yielding lower mean objective on dev_24 (currently 16.0201) with emphasis on the weakest regimes (capacity_level=tight, size=100, depot_style=eccentric), because tight-capacity instances are exactly where load-aware ruin selection changes the repair outcome. Stagnation gating (stagnation_ratio, iter_frac) adds deterministic pseudo-noise only when the LNS is stalling, preserving early convergence.
